# Tinkrum quick actions: presets and actions

A companion to the Tinkrum app-file guide (tinkrum-app-guide.md). Read it when an app needs a quick action: the steps of a quick action in `tools` use the actions below, and an `action` block can run a built-in preset by its id. Lines that mention Tink's rules or operations (`addTool`, "rule 45") are about Tink, the assistant inside Tinkrum: in an app file, write the quick action into `tools` as the guide shows.

## Quick-action presets
Add one with addTool {tool: {preset}} (rule 20). Each line: id “name”: its steps as stepId:action{parameters you may override in params; * = asked on every run}.
- visa-photo “Visa / ID photo”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → photo:image.idPhoto{spec*,maxKB*} → name:file.rename{template}
- document-packet “Application packet”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → crop:image.crop{aspect} → order:file.order → pdf:pdf.fromImages{pageSize,orientation,marginMm,fit,maxMB} → name:file.rename{template*} → share:out.share
- email-photos “Photos for email or upload”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → size:image.resize{mode,px} → compress:image.compress{maxKB*,format} → share:out.share
- sign-return “Sign and send back”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → fill:pdf.fillForm{flatten,whenNoFields} → sign:pdf.sign → share:out.share
- scan-document “Scan a document”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → look:scan.enhance{mode} → pdf:pdf.fromImages{pageSize,orientation,marginMm,fit,maxMB,textLayer} → name:file.rename{template*} → share:out.share
- scan-table-excel “Scan a table to Excel”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → look:scan.enhance{mode} → excel:ocr.toExcel{lang,scope}
- image-table-excel “Table picture to Excel”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → excel:ocr.toExcel{lang,scope}
- scan-doc-word “Scan a document to Word”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → look:scan.enhance{mode} → word:ocr.toWord{lang}
- image-doc-word “Document picture to Word”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → word:ocr.toWord{lang}
- combine-documents “Combine documents”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → merge:pdf.merge{imagePage} → pages:pdf.pages → name:file.rename{template*} → share:out.share
- pdf-too-big “PDF too big to upload”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → compress:pdf.compress{maxMB*,whenTooBig} → share:out.share
- receipt-archive “Receipt archive”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → compress:image.compress{maxKB,format} → name:file.rename{template} → save:file.save
- expense-report “Expense report: add a receipt”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → look:scan.enhance{mode} → pdf:pdf.fromImages{pageSize,orientation,marginMm,fit,maxMB} → add:file.addExisting{position} → merge:pdf.merge{imagePage} → name:file.rename{template} → save:file.save
- redact-screenshots “Hide parts of screenshots”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → stitch:image.stitch{direction,gapPx,background} → redact:image.redact{style} → share:out.share
- send-photos “Send many photos”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → jpg:image.convert{format,quality} → clean:image.stripMetadata → size:image.resize{mode,px} → zip:zip.create → name:file.rename{template*} → share:out.share
- video-too-big “Video too big to send”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → compress:video.compress{by,maxMB*,quality} → share:out.share
- join-videos “Join video clips”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → order:file.order → merge:video.merge
- video-frame “Save a photo from a video”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → frame:video.frame → save:out.saveToPhotos
- mute-video “Remove sound from videos”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → mute:video.mute
- video-background-music “Add background music”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → music:video.audio{originalVolume*,loop*}
- fix-video-rotation “Fix video rotation”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → rotate:video.rotate{degrees*}
- video-speed “Speed up or slow down video”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → speed:video.speed{factor*}
- vertical-video “Crop videos for portrait posts”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → crop:video.crop{ratio*}
- old-photos “Scan old photos”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → save:out.saveToPhotos
- print-id-photos “ID photos to print”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → photo:image.idPhoto{spec*,maxKB} → sheet:image.printSheet{sheet,guides}
- foreign-pdf “Translate a PDF into English”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → extract:pdf.extractText → translate:translate.text{from,to} → pdf:text.toPdf{pageSize,fontSize} → name:file.rename{template} → share:out.share
- foreign-paper “Translate paper documents into English”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → read:ocr.recognize{lang*} → translate:translate.text{from,to} → pdf:text.toPdf{pageSize,fontSize} → name:file.rename{template} → share:out.share
- papers-to-english “Chinese documents into English”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → read:ocr.recognize{lang} → translate:translate.text{from,to} → pdf:text.toPdf{pageSize,fontSize} → name:file.rename{template} → share:out.share
- screenshot-translate “Translate screenshots”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → read:ocr.recognize{lang*} → translate:translate.text{from,to} → copy:text.copy
- audio-to-text “Recording to text”: pick:in.audio{source*,min,max} → text:audio.transcribe{lang*,model} → pdf:text.toPdf{pageSize,fontSize} → share:out.share
- merge-recordings “Join recordings into one”: pick:in.audio{source,min,max} → order:file.order → merge:audio.merge → name:file.rename{template*} → share:out.share
- voice-memo-archive “Voice memos by date”: pick:in.audio{source,min,max} → name:file.rename{template} → save:out.saveToFolder
- pdf-to-audio “PDF to audio”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → extract:pdf.extractText → speak:audio.fromText{lang,rate,format} → share:out.share
- pdf-doc-word “PDF to Word”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → pages:pdf.toImages{maxSide} → word:ocr.toWord{lang}
- pdf-doc-excel “PDF to Excel”: pick:in.files{accept,min,max} → pages:pdf.toImages{maxSide} → excel:ocr.toExcel{lang,scope}
- paper-to-audio “Read paper pages aloud”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → edges:scan.detect → read:ocr.recognize{lang} → speak:audio.fromText{lang,rate,format} → share:out.share
- video-srt-captions “Export video captions as SRT”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → captions:video.subtitles{lang*,model}
- mark-up-photos “Add arrows and notes to photos”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → mark:image.annotate
- brighten-photos “Brighten dark photos”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → adjust:image.adjust{mode,brightness,contrast,saturation}
- remove-photo-background “Remove a photo background”: pick:in.photos{source,min,max} → remove:image.removeBackground{background,color}
- normal-audio-volume “Make quiet audio easier to hear”: pick:in.audio{source,min,max} → volume:audio.volume{mode,db}
- normal-video-volume “Make quiet video easier to hear”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → volume:audio.volume{mode,db}
- denoise-audio “Reduce noise in a voice recording”: pick:in.audio{source,min,max} → denoise:audio.denoise
- denoise-video “Reduce noise in video speech”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → denoise:audio.denoise
- audio-too-big “Recording too big to send”: pick:in.audio{source,min,max} → compress:audio.compress{by,maxMB*,quality} → share:out.share
- cut-audio “Cut out part of a recording”: pick:in.audio{source,min,max} → trim:audio.trim → save:out.saveToFolder
- video-sound “Keep the sound of a video”: pick:in.videos{min,max} → sound:audio.fromVideo{format} → name:file.rename{template*} → save:out.saveToFolder

## Built-in tool catalog
Each action: id (input → output; start = an input action, same = the type it got) {parameters, ? = optional}: what it does. Use: the requests it answers and how to set it up. [local: X] = a step the user does by hand on the device (cropping, ordering, choosing pages, signing…): you only decide where it goes. [pack: X] = may need the X extension pack, which the app asks the user to download when the device has no built-in support.
- pdf (“PDF”): Merge, convert (images, Word, Excel, PowerPoint), compress, arrange, split, number, stamp, sign, fill in, unlock and password-protect PDFs on this device.
  - pdf.merge (files → pdf) {imagePage?: "a4"|"letter"|"fit", group?: "none"|"count"|"day"|"month", groupSize?: integer 1..50}: Merge PDFs and images into one PDF, in the order they were chosen. Each image becomes a page. group splits the files first and makes one PDF per group: "count" every groupSize files, "day" / "month" by the date taken (or modified).
  - pdf.fromImages (images → pdf) {pageSize: "a4"|"letter"|"fit", orientation: "auto"|"portrait"|"landscape", marginMm: number 0..30, fit: "contain"|"cover", maxMB: number 0..100, textLayer?: boolean, group?: "none"|"count"|"day"|"month", groupSize?: integer 1..50}: Put the images into one PDF (A4, Letter or the image size) with optional margins. Max size (MB) makes the PDF smaller by compressing the images; 0 = no limit. textLayer recognises the text on the device and adds it invisibly, so the PDF can be searched and copied from (Latin-script languages; needs the built-in text recognition). group makes one PDF per group instead: "count" every groupSize images, "day" / "month" by the date taken; max size then applies to each PDF.
  - pdf.compress (pdf → pdf) {maxMB: number 0.1..100, whenTooBig: "ask"|"images"|"keepText"}: Make existing PDFs smaller than a size by recompressing the pictures inside; text stays selectable. If that is not enough, whenTooBig decides: ask the user, turn the pages into pictures (text can no longer be selected), or keep the text and accept a bigger file. Use: To make existing PDFs smaller ("PDF too big to upload", "under 2 MB") use this with maxMB — never pdf.toImages followed by pdf.fromImages; it keeps the text selectable and asks the user before turning pages into pictures.
  - pdf.pages (pdf → pdf) {}: The user picks, removes, reorders and rotates pages on the device. [local: pages]
  - pdf.selectPages (pdf → pdf) {rule: "all"|"odd"|"even"|"first"|"last"|"range", range?: string}: Keep only some pages: all, odd, even, first, last or page numbers like 1-3, 5.
  - pdf.rotate (pdf → pdf) {angle: 90|180|270, rule: "all"|"odd"|"even"|"first"|"last"|"range", range?: string}: Rotate some or all pages clockwise.
  - pdf.split (pdf → pdf) {mode: "every"|"ranges", n?: integer 1..500, ranges?: string}: Split into several PDFs: every N pages, or by page ranges separated by ; (e.g. 1-3; 4-6).
  - pdf.pageNumbers (pdf → pdf) {position: "bottomCenter"|"bottomRight"|"bottomLeft"|"topCenter"|"topRight"|"topLeft", format: "n"|"nOfTotal"|"pageNOfTotal", startAt: integer 0..100000, fontSize: number 6..48, skipFirst: boolean}: Add page numbers to every page.
  - pdf.stamp (pdf → pdf) {text: string, position: "bottomCenter"|"bottomRight"|"bottomLeft"|"topCenter"|"topRight"|"topLeft"|"center", fontSize: number 6..120, color: "#000000"|"#C92A2A"|"#1864AB"|"#868E96", opacity: integer 10..100, angle: 0|45|-45, rule: "all"|"odd"|"even"|"first"|"last"|"range", range?: string}: Stamp a line of text (e.g. COPY, Confidential, or the date with {date}) on pages.
  - pdf.toImages (pdf → images) {maxSide: integer 400..4000}: Turn every page into a JPG image (long side in pixels). [pack: pdfview]
  - pdf.fromDocument (files → pdf) {pageSize: "a4"|"letter"}: Turn Word, Excel and PowerPoint files (also RTF) into PDFs on this device. Use: Word, Excel or PowerPoint to PDF → in.files with accept "documents" then this (on Android only Word works; say so in a note when they mention Excel or PowerPoint).
  - pdf.extractText (pdf → text) {}: Reads the text of a PDF, scanned pages included (pages without a text layer are read with text recognition, which may get some characters wrong). [pack: pdfview]
  - pdf.annotate (pdf → pdf) {start: "text"|"note"|"pen"|"highlight"|"box"|"erase"|"mosaic"}: A local editor shows each page; the user adds text (size, angle, color, movable), notes, arrows, boxes, freehand strokes, highlights, erasing and mosaic, and can undo. Use: "Mark up a PDF / highlight / underline / draw on a PDF / write a note on a PDF" → this, a local editor when running; the user draws on the pages on the device, without sending anything to AI. [local: annotate; pack: pdfview]
  - pdf.sign (pdf → pdf) {}: The user draws or picks a saved signature and places it on a page. [local: sign; pack: pdfview]
  - pdf.fillForm (pdf → pdf) {flatten: boolean, whenNoFields?: "stop"|"skip"}: The user fills in the PDF form fields on the device; flatten makes them uneditable. [local: fillForm]
  - pdf.unlock (files → same) {}: For each PDF that needs a password to open, the user types it on the device (or skips that file); the result has no password, so later steps can merge, compress or sign it. Use: PDFs that need a password to open (payslips, bank statements; "remove / unlock the password") → right after choosing them, before any other PDF step (the user types each password on the device). iPhone only for now: say so in a note when the user mentions Android.
  - pdf.protect (pdf → pdf) {}: Adds a password needed to open the PDFs. Use: "Add a password / protect the PDF" → the last step before sharing or saving (the password is asked on every run and is never a parameter). iPhone only for now: say so in a note when the user mentions Android.
- image (“Images”): Compress, convert (HEIC to JPG too), resize, crop, rotate and clean photos; stitch, grid, animated GIFs, hide parts, watermark and make ID photos, on this device.
  - image.annotate (images → images) {}: A local editor lets the user place text, arrows, outline boxes and freehand strokes on each photo, choose colors and undo. Use: "Draw arrows / outline boxes / write labels / mark up a photo" → this, a local editor when running; the user places marks and types labels on the device, without sending them to AI. [local: annotate]
  - image.adjust (images → images) {mode: "auto"|"manual", brightness: number -100..100, contrast: number 0..200, saturation: number 0..200}: Improve photos locally with automatic color adjustment or manual brightness (-100 to 100, neutral 0), contrast and saturation (0 to 200, neutral 100). Use: "Photo too dark / brighten / contrast / saturation / auto improve photo" → this; mode auto ignores the manual values.
  - image.removeBackground (images → images) {background: "transparent"|"color", color: string}: Keep the main subjects and remove the background locally, producing PNG with transparency or a solid color. Use: "Remove a photo background / cut out / white background" → this; mention the iOS 17+ / Google Play services requirement and the first model download. For an ID photo, the background of image.idPhoto replaces this step (rule 36); the user must still check the official requirements.
  - image.convert (images → images) {format: "jpeg"|"png"|"webp", quality: integer 10..100}: Convert HEIC, PNG or WebP photos to JPG, PNG or WebP. Use: "HEIC to JPG" → format "jpeg".
  - image.resize (images → images) {mode: "longEdge"|"width"|"height"|"percent"|"fit", px?: integer 16..12000, width?: integer 16..12000, height?: integer 16..12000, percent?: integer 1..100}: Make images smaller by long edge, width, height, percent or to fit a box.
  - image.compress (images → images) {maxKB: integer 10..50000, format: "jpeg"|"webp"}: Make each image at most the given size (KB) by lowering quality first, then size.
  - image.crop (images → images) {aspect: "free"|"1:1"|"4:3"|"3:4"|"3:2"|"2:3"|"16:9"|"9:16"|"35:45"|"33:48"}: The user frames each image on the device; the ratio can be locked (1:1, 4:3, 35:45 passport…). [local: crop]
  - image.rotate (images → images) {angle: 0|90|180|270, flip: "none"|"horizontal"|"vertical"}: Rotate clockwise and/or flip every image.
  - image.stripMetadata (images → images) {}: Remove location, camera and other hidden info.
  - image.stitch (images → images) {direction: "vertical"|"horizontal", gapPx: integer 0..80, background: "#FFFFFF"|"#000000"}: Join the images top to bottom (or side by side) into one long image, e.g. several screenshots.
  - image.toGif (images → images) {delayMs: integer 100..5000, maxSide: integer 160..1200}: Turn the images (at most 50, in their current order) into one animated GIF that loops, each image shown for the chosen time. Use: "Make an animated GIF from photos" → in.photos then this.
  - image.grid (images → images) {columns: integer 2..4, cell: "1:1"|"3:4"|"4:3", gapPx: integer 0..80, background: "#FFFFFF"|"#000000"}: Arrange the images in a grid (2–4 columns, same-size cells, centered crop) as one image.
  - image.redact (images → images) {style: "blur"|"black"}: The user draws boxes over private parts (names, numbers, faces); they are blurred or blacked out. [local: redact]
  - image.watermark (images → images) {text: string, mode: "corner"|"tile", corner: "bottomRight"|"bottomLeft"|"topRight"|"topLeft"|"center", sizePercent: integer 5..80, opacity: integer 10..100, color: "#FFFFFF"|"#000000"|"#868E96"|"#C92A2A"}: Put a line of text on the images, in a corner or repeated across (e.g. "For visa application only").
  - image.idPhoto (images → images) {spec: "us-passport"|"cn-visa"|"schengen"|"uk-passport"|"ca-passport"|"jp-passport"|"in-visa"|"cn-1inch"|"cn-2inch", maxKB: integer 0..5000, background?: "keep"|"white"|"blue"|"red"|"gray"|"custom", color?: string, autoCenter?: boolean}: The user frames the face at the required shape; the photo is cut to the official size in pixels (300 dpi) as a JPG, and kept under the size limit if the spec has one. background replaces everything but the person with white, blue, red, light grey or a custom color (needs iOS 15+, or Google Play services on Android). autoCenter finds the face on the device and starts the frame with the head at the size the spec asks for; the user still checks and adjusts it. [local: crop]
  - image.printSheet (images → images) {sheet: "4x6"|"5x7"|"a4"|"letter", guides: boolean}: Repeat each ID photo on a sheet of photo paper (4×6 in etc.) with cut lines, ready to print at a photo shop.
- video (“Video”): Make videos smaller, convert them to MP4, trim them and turn them into GIFs, on this device.
  - video.subtitles (video → files) {lang: "zh"|"zh-TW"|"en"|"ja"|"ko"|"fr"|"de"|"es"|"pt"|"it"|"ru"|"vi", model: "standard"|"fast"}: Recognize speech in each video on this device and export a separate UTF-8 .srt file with timestamps. Choose the spoken language; the first run may need a speech model download. Use: "Automatic video captions / export SRT subtitles" → this, lang = the spoken language. It DOES NOT burn text into video or return a subtitled video: say this clearly, especially when the user asks to add captions to the picture. [pack: speech-whisper-small]
  - video.speed (video → video) {factor: number 0.5..4}: Play each video at 0.5×–4× speed and export an MP4. Use: "Speed up / slow motion / 2x" → factor; note that the pitch changes and slow motion is not smooth.
  - video.crop (video → video) {ratio: "9:16"|"1:1"|"4:5"|"16:9"}: Center-crop each video to 9:16, 1:1, 4:5 or 16:9. Use: "Crop to portrait / square / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 / 16:9" → ratio.
  - video.rotate (video → video) {degrees: 90|180|270}: Rotate each video clockwise by 90, 180 or 270 degrees, relative to its displayed orientation. iPhone keeps the encoded video and changes its transform; Android re-encodes. Use: "Rotate / upside-down video" → degrees (270 turns left).
  - video.audio (video → video) {originalVolume: integer 0..100, loop: boolean}: Choose a music file locally when this runs, then use it as the soundtrack for each video. Use: "Replace / add background music" → in.videos then this (the music is chosen at run time). Never add a second input action for the music.
  - video.mute (video → video) {}: Remove all sound from each video and export an MP4 with no audio track. Use: "Remove all sound / mute a video" → in.videos then this.
  - video.frame (video → images) {}: Choose a time in each video on the device and save the nearest decoded frame as a full-resolution JPEG, upright. Use: "Save a photo / grab a frame from a video" → in.videos, this, optionally out.saveToPhotos. [local: frameMedia]
  - video.merge (video → video) {}: Join 2–10 videos in order into one MP4. Use: "Join / merge several video clips" → in.videos (min 2, max 10), file.order, this.
  - video.compress (video → video) {by: "size"|"quality", maxMB: number 1..2000, quality: "1080p"|"720p"|"480p"}: Make each video smaller: by size (at most N MB; the resolution drops as needed) or by quality (1080p / 720p / 480p). Use: "A video too big to send / make the video smaller / under N MB" → by "size" with maxMB, or by "quality".
  - video.convert (video → video) {format: "mp4"}: Convert videos (MOV, HEVC…) to MP4 with H.264 so that other people can open them; quality and resolution stay about the same. Use: "Others can't open it / MOV, HEVC or MKV to MP4".
  - video.toGif (video → images) {width: integer 160..800, fps: integer 4..20}: Turn each video into an animated GIF (at most 30 seconds; put "Trim" before it for a longer video). GIFs have no sound and get large quickly: a smaller width and fewer frames per second keep them small. Use: "Turn a video (clip) into a GIF" → in.videos, video.trim, then this.
  - video.trim (video → video) {}: The user picks the start and end of each video on the device; only that part is kept (no re-encoding, so it is quick and keeps the quality). Use: "Cut out a part / trim". The result is always MP4. [local: trimMedia]
- audio (“Audio”): Turn recordings into text and text into speech, record, make audio smaller, convert, trim and join it, on this device.
  - audio.denoise (audio|video → same) {}: Reduce background noise around speech in audio or video on this device with RNNoise. Use: "Reduce speech noise / noisy voice recording" → this; mention that it is for speech and may suppress music.
  - audio.volume (audio|video → same) {mode: "normal"|"db", db: number -24..24}: Adjust audio or video sound locally. Normal aims for -16 LUFS; manual changes gain in dB. Use: "Too quiet / normal volume" → mode "normal", db 0; explicit ±dB → mode "db", db as asked.
  - audio.transcribe (audio → text) {lang: "zh"|"zh-TW"|"en"|"ja"|"ko"|"fr"|"de"|"es"|"pt"|"it"|"ru"|"vi", model: "standard"|"fast"}: Turn recordings into text on this device (one language per run). Use: "Turn a recording into text / transcribe / notes from a lecture or meeting recording" → lang = the language spoken, usually followed by text.toPdf or text.toFile. [pack: speech-whisper-small]
  - audio.compress (audio → audio) {by: "size"|"quality", maxMB: number 0.1..2000, quality: "high"|"standard"|"voice"}: Make each recording smaller as an M4A: by size (at most N MB) or by quality (high / standard / voice, mono). Use: "A recording too big to send / under N MB" → by "size" with maxMB, or by "quality".
  - audio.convert (audio → audio) {format: "m4a"|"wav"|"mp3"}: Convert recordings and music (M4A, WAV, MP3, AMR, CAF, FLAC…) to M4A, which plays everywhere, to MP3 (for old players and car stereos), or to uncompressed WAV. Use: "Convert to M4A / WAV / MP3" → format.
  - audio.trim (audio → audio) {}: The user picks the start and end of each recording on a waveform; only that part is kept, as an M4A. Use: "Cut out a part / a ringtone" (local step on a waveform; an iPhone app can't set ringtones, so say so in a note when they ask for one). [local: trimMedia]
  - audio.merge (audio → audio) {}: Join the recordings into one M4A, in their current order (put "Order" before it to change the order). Use: "Join several recordings into one" → file.order then this.
  - audio.fromVideo (video → audio) {format: "m4a"|"wav"|"mp3"}: Save only the sound of each video as an audio file (M4A, MP3, or uncompressed WAV). Use: "Keep the sound / music of a video" (also "video to MP3") → in.videos then this (format "mp3" when they say MP3).
  - audio.fromText (text → audio) {lang: "auto"|"zh-Hans"|"en"|"zh-Hant"|"ja"|"ko"|"fr"|"de"|"es"|"pt"|"it"|"ru"|"vi"|"th"|"id"|"ar"|"tr"|"nl"|"pl"|"uk"|"hi", rate: number 0.5..2, format: "m4a"|"wav"}: Read the text aloud with the phone’s own voice on this device and save it as an audio file (M4A or WAV). Use: "Read a PDF / paper document / text aloud as an audio file, listen to it instead of reading, text to speech" → after the step that gets the text (pdf.extractText, scan.detect → ocr.recognize, in.text, translate.text); lang "auto" unless they name the language, rate 1 unless they want it slower or faster, format "m4a" unless they ask for WAV; then out.share or out.saveToFolder. It only makes an audio file with the phone's own voice (no player, no highlighting, no AI voices); a sentence they type in the request and want read out is an errand.
- scan (“Scanner”): Turn photos of paper into straight, clean pages and PDFs on this device.
  - scan.detect (images → images) {flatten?: boolean}: Finds the edges of the paper in each photo; the user checks or drags the four corners; then the page is straightened. Pages from the document camera are already straight and pass through. flatten (on unless false) also flattens curved or creased pages so the lines of text come out straight (needs a one-time model download; scanning works without it). [local: corners; pack: scan]
  - scan.enhance (images → images) {mode: "auto"|"gray"|"bw"|"none"}: Makes scanned pages easier to read: removes shadows, turns the paper white and straightens slightly tilted text.
- ocr (“Text recognition”): Get printed text out of photos and scans on this device, in 12 languages.
  - ocr.recognize (images → text) {lang: "auto"|"eng"|"chi_sim"|"chi_tra"|"jpn"|"kor"|"fra"|"deu"|"spa"|"por"|"ita"|"rus"|"vie"}: Reads printed text in the images. lang "auto" (the default) reads Chinese, Japanese, English and Western European text with one model and picks by the phone’s language otherwise; set a language only when the user names one. [pack: ocr]
  - ocr.toExcel (images → files) {lang: "auto"|"eng"|"chi_sim"|"chi_tra"|"jpn"|"kor"|"fra"|"deu"|"spa"|"por"|"ita"|"rus"|"vie", scope: "all"|"tables"}: Reads tables with ruled lines in the images and makes one Excel workbook, a sheet per page. Use: "Photo / scan of a table to Excel, a spreadsheet from a paper table" → in.photos (source "scanner" for paper, then scan.detect → scan.enhance mode "auto"; library photos and screenshots go straight in) → ocr.toExcel; lang "auto" unless they name the language of the table, scope "all" unless they want only the tables. A scanned PDF: in.files accept "pdf" → pdf.toImages first. It makes one .xlsx with a sheet per page, which the user can check and edit on the result page; only tables with ruled lines (or only horizontal rules) become cells, everything else comes out as rows of text. Handwriting and tables without lines are not supported yet.
  - ocr.toWord (images → files) {lang: "auto"|"eng"|"chi_sim"|"chi_tra"|"jpn"|"kor"|"fra"|"deu"|"spa"|"por"|"ita"|"rus"|"vie"}: Reads the printed pages in the images and makes one Word document: headings, paragraphs, lists, tables with ruled lines and pictures, a page per image. Use: "Photo / scan of a document, letter or book page to Word" → in.photos (source "scanner" for paper, then scan.detect → scan.enhance mode "auto"; library photos and screenshots go straight in) → ocr.toWord; lang "auto" unless they name the language. A scanned PDF: in.files accept "pdf" → pdf.toImages first. It makes one .docx (a page per image) that the user can check and edit on the result page. For a digital PDF, use in.files accept "pdf" → pdf.toImages → ocr.toWord too: available source graphics and paper size are retained locally, while body text is reconstructed as editable paragraphs and tables. Exact fonts and reading order are not guaranteed.
- translate (“Translate”): Translate text, photos and PDFs on this device, in 20 languages. Plain text only, for understanding the meaning.
  - translate.text (text → text) {from: "auto"|"zh-Hans"|"en"|"zh-Hant"|"ja"|"ko"|"fr"|"de"|"es"|"pt"|"it"|"ru"|"vi"|"th"|"id"|"ar"|"tr"|"nl"|"pl"|"uk"|"hi", to: "zh-Hans"|"en"|"zh-Hant"|"ja"|"ko"|"fr"|"de"|"es"|"pt"|"it"|"ru"|"vi"|"th"|"id"|"ar"|"tr"|"nl"|"pl"|"uk"|"hi"}: Translate the text on this device (Apple Translation on iPhone, ML Kit on Android) into another language; the result is plain text, without the original layout.
- zip (“ZIP”): Make ZIP archives from files or photos, and unzip archives, on this device.
  - zip.create (files → zip) {group?: "none"|"count"|"day"|"month", groupSize?: integer 1..50}: Put all the files into one ZIP archive (photos are stored as they are; documents are compressed). group makes one ZIP per group instead: "count" every groupSize files, "day" / "month" by the date taken (or modified).
  - zip.extract (zip → files) {}: Take the files out of a ZIP archive (password-protected archives are not supported).
- qr (“QR code”): Make QR codes from text, and read QR codes in photos and screenshots, on this device.
  - qr.generate (text → images) {sizePx: integer 200..2000, ecc: "L"|"M"|"Q"|"H"}: Turn the text (a link, Wi-Fi details, contact) into a QR code image (PNG).
  - qr.read (images → text) {}: Find and read the QR code in each image.
- text (“Text”): Turn typed or pasted text into a PDF or a text file, on this device.
  - text.toPdf (text → pdf) {pageSize: "a4"|"letter", fontSize: number 8..24}: Lay the text out on pages as a PDF (system fonts, so Chinese and Japanese work).
  - text.toFile (text → files) {}: Save the text as a .txt file (UTF-8).
  - text.toDocx (text → files) {}: Save the text as a Word file (.docx): a blank line starts a new paragraph.
  - text.copy (text → same) {}: Copy the text to the clipboard.
  - text.tidy (text → same) {blankLines: "keep"|"single"|"remove", spaces: boolean}: Remove extra spaces (at line ends, repeated spaces and tabs) and blank lines: blankLines "remove" drops them all, "single" keeps one between paragraphs, "keep" leaves them.
  - text.replace (text → same) {find: string, replaceWith: string, ignoreCase: boolean}: Replace every occurrence of a word or phrase with another, exactly as typed (not a pattern).
  - text.extract (text → same) {kind: "phone"|"email"|"url"|"number"|"date"}: Keep only every phone number, e-mail address, web address, number or date found in the text, one per line (dates as YYYY-MM-DD, numbers without thousands separators).
  - text.lines (text → same) {mode: "split"|"join", separator: "newline"|"comma"|"semicolon"|"space"|"tab"|"none"}: mode "split": cut the text at each separator (comma, semicolon, space or tab; Chinese commas count too) and put each part on its own line. mode "join": put all non-empty lines on one line, joined by the separator (newline, comma, semicolon, space, tab, or none).
- print (“Reports”): Turn the records in your data tables into a PDF report, list or receipt to share or print.
  - print.records (records → pdf) {template: "table"|"cards"|"receipt", title: string, fields: string[], pageSize: "a4"|"letter", attachments?: boolean}: Make a PDF from the records with a fixed template: table, cards, or receipt (table with a total of the first money field). The values are filled in on the device; only the template, title and field names are settings. Use: Set attachments: true when the user wants the receipts, photos or files of the records in the report ("with the receipts attached"). That is the only thing you choose: the files themselves are read on the device and you never see them.

Core actions available to every quick action:
- in.photos (start → images) {source: "library"|"files"|"camera"|"scanner", min: integer 1..50, max: integer 1..50}: Pick photos from the library or from the Files app (pictures downloaded or sent from a computer), take them with the camera, or scan paper with the document camera (finds the edges, captures automatically, several pages, already straightened; where it is not available, the camera is used). Use: Pictures from the Files app → source "files". To scan paper → source "scanner" followed by scan.detect (it passes pages from the document camera through and straightens camera photos on devices without one).
- in.files (start → depends on params) {accept: "pdf"|"images"|"pdfOrImages"|"zip"|"videos"|"audio"|"documents"|"any", min: integer 1..50, max: integer 1..50}: Pick files from the Files app (PDFs, images, videos, audio, Word / Excel / PowerPoint documents, or any file).
- in.videos (start → video) {source?: "library"|"files", min: integer 1..10, max: integer 1..10}: Pick videos from the photo library, or from the Files app (downloaded or copied from a computer: MP4, MOV, and on Android also MKV, WEBM, AVI); up to 10, each up to 4 GB. Use: Videos start here: source "library" for the photo library, "files" for videos downloaded or copied from a computer (MKV, WEBM, AVI only open on Android).
- in.audio (start → audio) {source: "files"|"record", min: integer 1..10, max: integer 1..10, autoStart?: boolean}: Pick recordings or music from the Files app (up to 10, each up to 4 GB), or record one now with the microphone (it keeps recording when the screen locks). Use: Audio starts here: source "files" for recordings and music in the Files app, "record" to record now with the microphone (autoStart: true starts recording as soon as the screen opens and one tap on Stop hands the recording on, for "say it and go" flows); shared recordings fill it either way.
- in.text (start → text) {text: string}: The user types or pastes text (for a QR code or a text PDF). The text stays on this device.
- in.wifi (start → text) {network: string, security: "WPA"|"WEP"|"none", hidden: boolean}: The user enters a Wi-Fi network (name, security, password); the result is the text phones read from a Wi-Fi QR code (follow with qr.generate).
- in.records (start → records) {collectionId: string, period: "all"|"today"|"thisWeek"|"thisMonth"|"thisYear"|"last7days"|"last30days"|"last14days"|"last90days"|"last365days"|"thisTwoWeeks"|"thisHalfMonth"|"next7days"|"next30days"|"next90days"|"yesterday"|"lastWeek"|"lastMonth"|"lastYear"|"tomorrow"|"nextWeek"|"nextMonth"}: Take the records of one data table (optionally only a time period, by its first date field).
- out.addRecord (files|text → same) {collectionId: string, each?: boolean, into?: "new"|"existing"}: Hand the files (or the text) to a new record in a data table: the files are saved in Tinkrum and go into the table's first attachment field (up to 20), text goes into its first long-text or text field, and the user checks the form and fills in the other fields (amount, category…) while the quick action runs; date fields start as today. With into “existing” it makes no new entry: when it runs the user picks an existing entry of the table, the files go after the files already in it (an entry holds at most 20), the text goes into the field when it is empty or on a new line after what is there, and the user checks the entry’s form and saves. Use: A button that scans into a table ("scan receipts into my expenses") → in.photos source "scanner", scan.detect, out.addRecord. The form reads the attachments on the device and suggests values by itself, so add no ocr step for that. All the files go into one record; each: true only when the user wants one record per file ("one entry per receipt"). To put the result into an entry that is already there ("add it to an existing entry", "append to a record") set into: "existing": the user picks the entry when it runs; leave each out. [local: recordEntry]
- file.rename (files|images|pdf|zip → same) {template: string}: Name the result with a template such as {sourceName}-{date}. {ocr:RULE} / {qr:RULE} put in a part of the text recognized in each photo on the device / of its QR code; RULE is firstLine, invoiceNo, date, amount, phone, email, url or number.
- file.order (files → same) {}: The user puts the files in order and can drop some, on the device. [local: reorder]
- file.filter (files → same) {kind: "any"|"images"|"pdf"|"video"|"audio"|"documents", size: "any"|"larger"|"smaller", sizeMB?: number 0.01..4096, orientation: "any"|"landscape"|"portrait"|"square", date: "any"|"lastDays"|"period"|"between", days?: integer 1..3650, period?: "today"|"thisWeek"|"thisMonth"|"thisYear"|"last7days"|"last30days"|"last14days"|"last90days"|"last365days"|"thisTwoWeeks"|"thisHalfMonth"|"next7days"|"next30days"|"next90days"|"yesterday"|"lastWeek"|"lastMonth"|"lastYear"|"tomorrow"|"nextWeek"|"nextMonth", from?: string, to?: string, duration: "any"|"longer"|"shorter", seconds?: number 1..86400, whenEmpty: "stop"|"skip"}: Keep only the files that meet every condition set here (the others are dropped from this run, never deleted): kind of file; size larger / smaller than N MB; photo orientation (landscape, portrait, square); date taken (or last modified) in the last N days or between two dates; video or audio length longer / shorter than N seconds. A file whose date, size in pixels or length can’t be read does not meet that condition. whenEmpty: "stop" ends the run with a message when nothing is left, "skip" passes all the files on unfiltered.
- file.addExisting (files → files) {position: "before"|"after"}: Asks which earlier file to add to the files so far: by default the last result this quick action saved, or a PDF or image picked in Files, or none this time. position "before" puts the existing file first. Use: To add new pages to a PDF made before ("add this receipt to last time's expense report", "keep one growing PDF") → this (position "before") then pdf.merge, after the new pages; the user picks the earlier file when it runs (by default the last result this quick action saved, so end with file.save).
- file.save (files → same) {}: Save the result to the files in this app.
- out.share (files → same) {}: Open the share sheet once with all the files (WeChat, WhatsApp, Mail, Messages, AirDrop, Files…). Use: "Send to X" (WeChat, WhatsApp, Mail…) → this: it opens the share sheet once with all the files and the user picks. Tinkrum never uploads files or sends them to a contact by itself.
- out.saveToFolder (files → same) {}: Copy the files into a folder in Files (on this device, iCloud Drive, Google Drive, Dropbox…). Use: "Put them in my cloud drive / a folder" → this: the user picks a folder in Files, which is also how files reach iCloud Drive, Google Drive or Dropbox.
- out.saveToPhotos (images|video → same) {}: Save the images or videos to the photo library.
- out.print (pdf|images → same) {}: Print with AirPrint or a system printer.
- out.call (text → same) {}: Open the phone app with this number.
- out.message (text → same) {}: Open the messages app with this number.
- out.email (text → same) {}: Open a new email to this address.
- out.website (text → same) {}: Open this web address in the browser, after asking first.
- records.toVCard (records → files) {}: Make one contact file (.vcf) from the records.
- records.toVCardText (records → text) {}: Make the text of a contact card (vCard) from the records, to chain into a QR code.
- records.toExcel (records → files) {collectionId?: string, fields?: string|"createdAt"[], attachments?: boolean}: Make one Excel file (.xlsx) from the records, named after the table: one column per field, with the field names on the first row. Use: "Export to Excel" → in.records, this, out.share. fields is an ordered list of field IDs (createdAt allowed; updatedAt is not supported); empty or missing preserves all columns. Bind collectionId for handed records when selecting fields. attachments returns the Excel plus attachment copies, optionally chain zip.create. No charts or pivots.
- records.fill (records → depends on params) {collectionId: string, templatesTable: string, kind: "text"|"word"|"email", body?: string[], subject?: string[], document?: string[], recipient?: string[]}: Fill a user-written text, Word or email template with exactly one entry, on this device. Use: Bind collectionId. Accept records from recordRow, single blocks, lists or in.records. If several entries arrive, ask the user to select exactly one, then fill once; never generate Word files or emails in bulk. Templates are ordinary entries written by the user in templatesTable: configure body/subject/document as one-element field ID arrays; recipient names one email-format field in collectionId. Never compose template content or see it. User placeholders are {Field name}, replaced locally. kind is fixed, not asked at run time: text → text, word → files, email → text: opens one email draft and returns the filled body; further text actions may follow. Only Excel exports many entries at once; template filling always works on one entry selected by the user. Names use the template entry title and existing file.rename; no new naming placeholders.

## Rules for quick actions
15. Name templates may only use these placeholders: {date} or {date:FORMAT} where FORMAT uses YYYY MM DD HH mm ss and - _ . ; {index}; {seq} (01, 02…); {sourceName}; {taken} or {taken:FORMAT} (the photo's capture date). The word "date" means {date:YYYY-MM-DD}. Keep the user's literal words, e.g. "merged-date" → "merged-{date:YYYY-MM-DD}".
20. Building quick actions: Pick actions from the catalog below whose input accepts the previous step's output; start with an input action (rule 54 is the only exception); use the user's numbers exactly (sizes in KB/MB, 1 MB = 1024 KB; pixels, page sizes). Give every parameter the action lists. Follow the "Use:" notes in the catalog: they say which action answers which request and how to set it up. Local steps only say where the user works by hand. When the user asks for something a preset already does ("visa photo", "scan a document"), add it with addTool {tool: {preset}}: the app fills in the preset's steps exactly as the user would get them; put only the parameters the user asks to change in params, by step id (no params when they change nothing) (e.g. {"op": "addTool", "tool": {"preset": "visa-photo", "params": {"photo": {"maxKB": 100}}}}), and give id or name only for a second copy. Write the steps yourself (addTool {tool: {kind: "quickAction", id, name, steps}}) only when no preset does the job. "Put X on the home page" → addContainer an action block {look: "action", tools: [{tool: "<id>"}]} on "home"; the id may be a preset id (the built-in quick action is used as is, nothing to add), otherwise add the quick action first if it doesn't exist yet. Never add an action block the user didn't ask for: when you create a quick action, the app itself asks the user whether to put it on the home page. If the user says not to put it there, set "homeEntry": false on the plan. Adding a processing step (addTool {tool, step, index}) goes before the final naming / saving / sharing steps. Results always end on a result page with save, share, save-to-folder and print buttons, so a final out.share, out.saveToFolder or file.save is only needed when the user asks for it. What the user says beats a preset's defaults: when they want English and the preset translates into Chinese, set that step's parameter in params and give a name that says what it now does.
21. Reports from records: a quick action in.records {collectionId, period} → print.records {template, title, fields, pageSize} turns the user's records into a PDF on the device (action parameters call a table collectionId). You choose only the table, the time period, the template ("table", "cards", or "receipt" = table with a total of the first money field), the title and field ids — you never see or quote the records. Questions about what the records contain are still rejected with "userData". Records from files: a quick action ending in out.addRecord {collectionId} (e.g. in.photos source "camera" → out.addRecord, "snap a receipt and log it") adds one record per file while it runs: the file goes into the table's first file field (addData a file field first if the table has none), text into its first note or text field, and the user fills in the other fields on a form at run time. Building that quick action is a change to the app; typing the entry's content yourself is still "userData".
22. Goals instead of instructions: users often say what they have and what they want ("two photos of my ID card, the school wants one PDF under 2 MB") instead of listing steps. Build the quick action that gets them there, choosing steps for the purpose: sending by email or to a website → compress or resize images first (several large photos easily pass the usual 20–25 MB attachment limit); sending to a school, office or accountant, or filing things every month → name the file with the date; paper documents, receipts and contracts → scan (in.photos). Don't add steps the goal doesn't need (no manual crop for receipts the scanner already straightens; no watermark or redaction unless asked). Then write "notes" for the preview — at most 2, each one short sentence (under 40 Chinese characters or 20 English words) in the interface language — only for what the user would otherwise get wrong: a part of their goal the app can't do (there are no scheduled or automatic runs, so "every month" means they tap it each month; the app can't send to a specific person by itself, the share sheet opens and they pick), or a step you added that they didn't name and why ("compressed so it fits in an email"). Don't restate the steps (the preview lists them) and don't add general disclaimers. Leave notes out when there is nothing like that to say. Only reject a goal when nothing useful in it can be built. Steps the user names are always built as they ask, in their order, even when they look unnecessary or odd, as long as each step accepts the previous step's output (a chain that ends in out.addRecord hands the result to a form the user confirms): never reject or leave them out for being unreasonable; at most one note says why it may not help.
28. Keeping only some files ("only the photos from the last 7 days", "skip files over 10 MB", "only landscape photos", "videos shorter than a minute") → file.filter right after the input step: set only the conditions the user names (kind, size larger/smaller than sizeMB, orientation, date lastDays with days, period (thisWeek, thisMonth… — use it for "this month" so it stays right next month) or between from/to as YYYY-MM-DD, duration longer/shorter than seconds) and leave the rest at "any"; all conditions must hold. whenEmpty "stop" (default) ends the run with a message when nothing is left, "skip" passes every file on unfiltered. It drops files from this run only; it never deletes anything (a request to delete files is still "deleteFiles"). It can't look at what is in a file (people, words): reject that part with "unknown".
29. One result per group ("one PDF per day", "a PDF for every 10 photos", "zip each month separately") → set group on the step that makes the files: pdf.fromImages, pdf.merge or zip.create, with group "count" + groupSize, "day" or "month" (by date taken, or modified for files from Files). Each group becomes one PDF / ZIP named after its date (or its first file), so a later file.rename with {sourceName} keeps the date. There are no loops: never repeat steps per group, and grouping by anything else (people, content, folders) can't be done — reject that part with "unknown".
30. Names from what is in the photo ("name each receipt by its invoice number", "name the tickets by the phone number in their QR code"): besides the placeholders of rule 15, a file.rename template may use {ocr:RULE} (text recognized in that photo on the device) and {qr:RULE} (its QR code), where RULE is one of firstLine, invoiceNo, date (written as YYYY-MM-DD), amount (the total), phone, email, url, number. Set ask: [] on that step (a name typed at run time replaces the template). Only these rules exist: never invent another rule or write a pattern; you never see the text. When a part isn't found it is left out, and the original name is used if nothing is left. Text recognition runs only for photos, not PDFs.
31. Working on text inside a quick action (after in.text, ocr.recognize, qr.read, pdf.extractText, audio.transcribe or translate.text): "remove blank lines / extra spaces" → text.tidy; "replace X with Y" → text.replace with the user's literal words in find and replaceWith (never a pattern; they become "<user text>" when you see them again — leave them unchanged); "get all the phone numbers / e-mails / links / numbers / dates" → text.extract with that kind; "one item per line" / "put the lines together" → text.lines split or join with the separator they name. These change the app; the text itself still never reaches you, so writing, summarizing or translating a text the user typed in the request is still an errand (rule 24).
54. A container hands its data to its tools when the user taps (nothing runs on opening a page; you never run them and never see the values). Such a quick action has no input step: it starts with a step that takes text or records, and it only works where that is handed over. Three layers. A value (one field): an item {tool, field} in a table's recordRow, the row of buttons at the top of its entry page; built-in tools with no addTool needed are record-call, record-message, record-email, record-website (they show only when the field has the matching format and a valid value, so set format on the field) and record-copy, or your own quick action starting with a step that takes text (text.copy, qr.generate). This entry: an item {tool} with no field in recordRow (built-in record-vcard, record-qr, or your own starting with records.toVCard, records.toExcel, print.records with empty fields), or {tool} on a single block. The records of a list: {as: "list", tool} (up to 3) on a list, cards or checklist block, which hands over everything the list currently selects, its filter and search, not cut to limit. "add a call button to contacts" → updateData {table, changes: {recordRow: [{tool: "record-call", field: "phone"}]}} (order = button order; a table without recordRow has no row; repeat a tool for a second phone field). "export what I searched", an export button on a list → as "list". A tool that should work from anywhere ("export all my contacts" on the home page) keeps in.records as its first step instead. These quick actions cannot sit on an action or button block, in a reminder, on the phone home screen or on the file desk. Attachments: a quick action whose first step takes files (pdf.compress, image.resize, file.save…) and has no input step is handed the files of an attachment field, only the kinds that first step takes; an item {tool, field} in recordRow with field an attachment field, or {tool} on a single block or {as: "list", tool} on a list, which hand over the first attachment field of their table (up to 20 files, copies, the originals are never touched; you never see their names or contents). "compress this entry's PDF" → addTool {steps: [pdf.compress, out.share]} + recordRow {tool, field: <the attachment field>}. Once running, the files are just files: the quick action forgets which entry they came from and works like any other (add them to a record with out.addRecord when the user wants that). A quick action that lets the user pick files themselves keeps in.photos or in.files as its first step; a number, money, date, time, duration, rating, choice or tags field also hands over the text it shows to a step that takes text.
